t.2.74.1: Then came men who knew the lie of the land, those skilled in laying out lines with cord, brave workers devoted to their own tasks, diggers, and likewise engineers who worked machines.
t.2.74.3: Well-diggers, plasterers, and workers in bamboo, and those who were skilled overseers, set out in front.
t.2.74.2: Overseers of works, master builders, men skilled in machines, and carpenters too, along with road-makers and tree-fellers, set out.
t.2.74.4: Joyfully they went toward that place, and that vast flood of people, surging with great force, shone like the ocean at the full moon.
t.2.74.5: Those men, skilled in the work of road-making, each took up his own appointed post and set out ahead, equipped with tools of many kinds.
t.2.74.6: Those men made a road, cutting through creepers and vines, shrubs, tree stumps and rocks, and trees of many kinds.
t.2.74.7: In treeless regions some planted trees, while others, here and there, cut them down with axes, chisels and sickles.
t.2.74.8: Others, stronger still, cleared away the sturdy clumps of vīraṇa grass and leveled the rough, impassable places and the uneven ground here and there.
t.2.74.9: Others filled up the wells and the long pit with earth, and likewise some made the low-lying parts level on every side.
t.2.74.10: Then the men bound what needed binding and crushed what needed crushing, and in those various places they split apart what needed splitting.
t.2.74.11: In a very short time they made many reservoirs full of water, of many different shapes and resembling the ocean, and wells of many kinds adorned with raised platforms.
t.2.74.13: Sprinkled with sandalwood water and adorned with many kinds of flowers, the road for the army shone greatly, like the path to heaven.
t.2.74.12: Its surface was paved with stucco, its trees were in full bloom, it rang with the cries of flocks of excited birds, and it was adorned with banners.
t.2.74.14: Then those appointed officers, having issued orders according to their instructions, set to work in delightful regions abounding in many sweet fruits.
t.2.74.15: And the encampment that was desired by the great-souled Bharata, itself like an ornament, they adorned still further with decorations.
t.2.74.16: Under auspicious constellations and at favorable moments, those versed in that science established the encampment of the great-souled Bharata.
t.2.74.17: And there stood many ramparts of heaped earth, encircled by moats, resembling Indrakīla and adorned with splendid gateways.
t.2.74.19: With their lofty little mansions, crowned with dovecote turrets and seeming to glide through the sky, those settlements shone like the city of Śakra.
t.2.74.18: All of them were furnished with rows of palaces, enclosed by mansions and ramparts, adorned with banners, and laid out with well-built great highways.
t.2.74.21: Just as the spotless sky shines at night, adorned with the moon and hosts of stars, so did that royal highway shine, delightful, built step by step by skilled craftsmen.
t.2.74.20: Having reached the Jāhnavī, whose banks were wooded with many kinds of trees, whose water was cool and clear, and which teemed with great fish...
